turns.assessment: The outage is concentrated on lightpath och6, whose S17 receiver showed rising pre-FEC BER followed by OTU_LOF, while received power, estimated OSNR, DGD, SOP rate, and the line amplifiers remained unchanged. The earlier similar failure of och44 at S17 makes a channel-filter problem in the S17 ROADM more plausible than an isolated receiver failure, but the documented WSS filter fault is channel-specific and the evidence does not distinguish it decisively from receiver degradation or an upstream filter fault. No exact cause reaches the 80% commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: A shifted or narrowed passband explains BER growth and eventual LOF with unchanged optical power and estimated OSNR. Two channels terminating at S17, och44 and och6, degraded in succession, pointing toward the local ROADM; however, the documented mode normally affects only one channel.

Receiver-local degradation at trx.och6.a fits the increased BER and LOF while the optical path metrics remain normal. It does not naturally explain the similar earlier failure of och44 at the same site.

A filter penalty at the immediately upstream ROADM channel could degrade och6 without changing received power or aggregate line measurements, but the available observations do not identify that ROADM channel uniquely.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
